messages.author: 81b6b3d7dfea88a5
messages.subject: Re: mapBubbles: How to fit the size of the legend to the size of the graph or
parts:
Hi Christiane,

I'm guessing that you might be using RStudio (I use it too & recognise the name of the png).

Part of your problem is that the map is very small and so the legends are relatively large.

mapDevice() in rworldmap was designed to create a world map shaped window, but RStudio doesn't like it.

However if you are on windows putting this before your mapBubbles command should solve most of your problem. Someone else might want to suggest what works on linux ?
mapDevice("windows")

New Zealand is still covered up, that can be fixed by adding : legendHoriz=TRUE

Also I guess you might want to change the legend title by : legendTitle= " # of respondents"

As an afterthought, if you add : fill=FALSE,lwdSymbols=2, it solves the overlapping symbols in Europe and you can see that the largest bubbles are for the UK & Germany. 
The symbols can be irregular in a png but if you save as a pdf they look good (see attached).

mapParams <- mapBubbles(dF=sPDF ,nameZSize="Numberofrespondents", nameZColour="REGION", colourPalette="rainbow", oceanCol="lightblue",landCol="wheat",legendHoriz=TRUE, legendTitle=" # of respondents", fill=FALSE,lwdSymbols=2)

Best,
Andy
